findings.message: onCleanup is called without a reactive owner; no scope's disposal can trigger it, so this cleanup function will never run; the enclosing callback is owned only on its first run and runs with no owner on any later run, so solid-checker cannot prove every execution has an owner
findings.hint: Call onCleanup inside a component or computation, or create the surrounding scope with createRoot so disposal exists. For one-time setup with teardown, use onSettled with a returned cleanup in a component. Create owned work in the effect's compute, or keep the apply callback free of primitives and cleanups that a later run would leave detached.

findings.message: effect is created without a reactive owner; nothing will ever dispose it, so it keeps running and holding its subscriptions for the lifetime of the app; the enclosing callback is owned only on its first run and runs with no owner on any later run, so solid-checker cannot prove every execution has an owner
findings.hint: Create effects inside a component or computation so their owner disposes them. For deliberate module-scope reactivity, wrap the setup in createRoot(dispose => ...) and keep the dispose handle. Create owned work in the effect's compute, or keep the apply callback free of primitives and cleanups that a later run would leave detached.

findings.message: reactive accessor "shared" is read directly in createRenderEffect apply callback, which does not track; the read sees the current value once and never updates when "shared" changes
findings.hint: Move the read into a tracking scope: JSX, a createMemo, or the compute function of createEffect(compute, apply). If a one-time snapshot is intended, wrap the read in untrack() to make that explicit. Solid warns STRICT_READ_UNTRACKED here in dev.
